title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 27
description: Ten questions on Acts 27: the voyage toward Italy, the storm called Euroclydon, and the shipwreck from which all escaped safely.

questions.text: What was the name of the centurion to whom Paul and the other prisoners were delivered?
questions.explanation: When it was determined that they should sail for Italy, Paul and certain other prisoners were delivered to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

questions.text: Who went with them, described as a Macedonian of Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: They embarked in a ship of Adramyttium and put to sea, with Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with them.

questions.text: What did Julius allow Paul to do when they touched at Sidon?
questions.explanation: Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

answers.text: Buy food for the whole ship
Go to his friends and refresh himself

questions.text: What did Paul warn the voyage would bring?
questions.explanation: Paul said he perceived that the voyage would be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of their lives.

answers.text: A long delay in Crete, but no danger to anyone
Injury and much loss of the cargo, the ship and their lives
The loss of the cargo, but not of the ship
Shipwreck on the coast of Cilicia near Myra

questions.text: To whom did the centurion give more heed than to what Paul said?
questions.explanation: The centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to the things spoken by Paul.

answers.text: To the master and the owner of the ship
To the soldiers under his command
To the chief man of Crete

questions.text: What was the stormy wind called that beat down from shore?
questions.explanation: Before long a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

questions.text: What did the angel who stood by Paul that night tell him?
questions.explanation: The angel said, "Don't be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar," and that God had granted him all those who sailed with him.

answers.text: That the ship would reach Italy unharmed
Not to be afraid, because he must stand before Caesar
That he would be freed in Crete
That only the sailors would be saved

questions.text: What did the sailors find when they took soundings twice near midnight?
questions.explanation: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms, and after a little while they took soundings again and found fifteen fathoms.

answers.text: First fifteen fathoms, then twenty fathoms
First twenty fathoms, then fifteen fathoms

questions.text: How many souls does the text say were on the ship?
questions.explanation: The chapter says that in all they were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

questions.text: What did the centurion do when the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners?
questions.explanation: The soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, but the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose.

answers.text: He agreed and had them bound
He put the prisoners in the boat
He stopped them, because he wanted to save Paul
He left the decision to the ship's master
